mode: regression / fix-wave confirmation (story-026 depositFor settlement, story-027 Active gate)

resourceCaps.note: Prior attempt crashed the WSL2 host (unbounded solver processes). This run enforced, on EVERY invocation: --solver-threads 2 --solver-max-memory 512 --solver-timeout-assertion 60s --solver-timeout-branching 5s, wrapped in `systemd-run --user --scope -p MemoryMax=4G -p CPUQuota=400%`, one test contract at a time, strictly sequential, memory checked between runs. Containment verified live: the one runaway solver (yices-smt2, 2.3GB on SymbolicScheduleMath) was OOM-killed inside its cgroup with zero host impact.
resourceCaps.consequence: The 60s/assertion ceiling is tighter than prior ad-hoc runs; several nonlinear div/mul properties that are believed-true (and fuzz-held) TIMEOUT under it. Timeouts are recorded below with zero safety weight.

regressionTargetVerdict.story-026_depositFor_settlement: PROVEN on real bytecode (bounded domain): depositFor pays the STAKER exactly their pending, the migrator captures 0, post-call pending is 0 (no double-pay), and strong solvency `balance == rewardBudget + committedDebt` survives — for every elapsed time in [1s, 90 days] x every deposit amount in [1, 2^96) against a funded 1-month-window pool with a live position (15 execution paths, non-vacuous). The recipient-redirect accounting is additionally proven recipient-invariant and solvency-neutral in the arithmetic model (2^128 domains).

findings.description: DESIGNED witness, not a new finding: across two accrual epochs, pending (difference of two independently-floored snapshots) can exceed the user's true share of the second epoch's bump — the documented ~1-wei user-favouring rounding that _safePay's dust branch absorbs. The in-test comment declares this counterexample expected.
findings.caveat: The companion <=1-wei bound (ACC-3 / ACC-3b) did NOT prove this run (TIMEOUT under the 60s cap, both unbounded and bounded) — the excess being bounded by exactly 1 wei is fuzz-supported but not symbolically proven in run-22.

vacuousPasses.honestWeight: ZERO for their intended no-revert property
vacuousPasses.reason: Methodology probe (SymbolicRevertProbe, this run) PROVED that default halmos silently PRUNES external-call reverts instead of surfacing them: a harness call that certainly underflows (rb - amount with amount > rb reachable) still returns PASS. These four checks assert no-revert of an external harness call, so they are structurally incapable of failing — their PASS says nothing about revert reachability. Do NOT cite them as proof that _safePay cannot revert. The LOCAL-007 revert-window question stays with the fuzz campaign and manual reasoning.
vacuousPasses.action: Carried as a harness-defect note; if a future run needs a real no-revert proof, re-encode with try/catch capturing the revert into an assertable bool (as the run-22 gate tests do with low-level call).

methodologyFindings.title: Default halmos prunes external-call reverts — 'no-revert' checks are unfalsifiable
methodologyFindings.evidence: test/SymbolicRevertProbe.t.sol::check_probe_revertIsPruned: harness call with reachable checked-underflow returns PASS (2 paths, 0 models).
methodologyFindings.consequence: Downgraded 4 prior-session PASSes to zero weight (see vacuousPasses). Pattern for future runs: encode revert-reachability via low-level call + assert on the success flag, as SymbolicStakeGateV2 does.
